verdict.tagline: A slow survival build that asks a lot from early settlers.
for_you_if: you enjoy deep survival crafting systems
you want to build and manage medieval settlements
you appreciate extensive customization over starting hand-holding
not_for_you_if: you will not connect through Epic Services for co-op
you dislike heavy early grinds and tedious fetch quests
you want fully voiced dialogue for NPCs

distortion_flags.sentence: Player reception shifts dramatically from negative initial impressions during the refund window to positive evaluations over extended playtimes.

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Early impressions suffer from text-only dialogue, heavy grinding, crashes, and third-party service requirements for multiplayer.

claims.claim: NPC interactions feature text-only dialogue without audible voice acting.

citations.review_text: The UI is much too complicated considering the overall simplicity. Graphics are janky, even with a decent graphics card and processor. Lack of audible dialogue when interacting with NPCs makes for a story in which I cannot get immersed. Very little character customization was a disappointment before even starting the game. Overall, this game leaves a lot to be desired and I've requested a refund.  Let's hope Windrose is somewhat better.

it's a really fun game but it definetly has it's fair share of bugs. Notably, don't use Directx12 use 11. The game will crash using 12. Also it's a bit buggy sometimes and can get a fatal error crash. Otherwise It's got some great mechanics and the building side of it is really fun, Sidenote; The Characters Don't have dialogue voices, just text, It's not a deal breaker but it was a suprise.

There's probably a better game comparison that I've not played, but it's a bit like if Banished were in 3D, but you had to run across the countryside to fulfill the whims of a chat bot to have the ability to build anything.

Questioning the store tags....is it an "RPG" game with craft & build mechanics (template builds)?  Or is it a (limited) craft & build game with rpg-like quest restraints on progression?  It's neither.  It fails at both.  Good RPG games grab the player emotionally from the off, drag them in with a reason to play and a connection to certain NPCs.  The opening scenes didn't do that at all for me.  Good "building" games allow you creativity and don't lock progression behind poor rpg and template designs.

I've probably missed the intended point of the game entirely by giving up on it so soon, but to me it felt like Errand Simulator - And I could have got behind that if I didn't dislike the NPC interactions so much.  I'm not a fan of the voiceless, text-based dialogue, it does nothing to make me want to work with them.

Bonus:  motion sickness despite changing the settings that usually help.  This was what made me have to request a refund.

Well no voice acting that is a joke especially in the 2026 if i knew that i would not have bought it and no workshop and to me that means the debs are lazy or just f****** greedy....... yeah well thats a big fat NO from me :steamthumbsdown:

claims.claim: Co-op multiplayer requires connecting through Epic Services.

citations.review_text:
Despite devs saying it does not install EOS https://steamcommunity.com/app/1129580/discussions/0/3427823001996939764/?ctp=2#c3317484899034260947
it actually does.
You cannot play coop without connecting to Epic.
Unfortunately the game was in our lib for too long before we tried to play but we'll ask for a refund nevertheless.

Runs well and looks good, but game crashes at random intervals and all the quests are shared which makes first time playthroughs with other people really difficult since you have to repeatedly relay all the info the quest giver is telling you cause you only get told it once per group. Dissapointing, was very excited for this game for a long time

claims.claim: Resource gathering and early building require a heavy grind of repetitive tasks like collecting sticks and logs.

citations.review_text: the resource farming is way too slow. i want to play a game, not run back and forth between my unfinished storage hut and the forest with logs for hours.

Unfortunately it's really grindy. I played it for almost an hour and that whole hour was spent just picking up rocks and sticks, cutting down trees and holding left mouse on the blueprint of a house until it was built. I finished it and it instantly hits me with the next objective: Make some traps to catch some animals. How do you do that? Collect more sticks and rocks...

I was really hoping there would be more medieval gameplay and less grinding and micromanagement, but apparently it takes quite a while to really automate things. If you're into just slowly building up your resources and creating a village, then eventually seeing it pay off, this game is for you. For me, personally, I've already played Minecraft and it already scratched the itch that this game does.

The store page really needs some new materials to demonstrate how grindy and slow this game is.

Played in SIngleplayer

When i first saw the skill system i was expecting something akin to Valheim, get better at the things you do often, instead, you get a semi-generic perk point relevant to the thing you were doing. Like Skyrim but instead of having 18 skill trees entirely specific to the activity, you have 6 trees that are generally relevant. Gathering can level survival, which lets you buff up your poison resistance or axe condition...

Too much time investment is required for the basic buildings. about 80 total items of logs, sticks & 2 other things for the most basic house, which is your first shelter.

I didn't see a campfire in the quick build menu but the game references it in the tutorial.

The world felt empty, trees everywhere, a few villages sprinkled around but looking around just felt dull.

The NPCs had external monologues often but i don't think i heard the villagers actually communicate to each other. NPCs walk & stand like generic bots.

"Have you heard anything interesting" -> "I heard someone in X village requires your help" - WTF is that response. There was no deviation, i asked several NPCs & they all said the same thing. No tips about the wilderness, animal behaviours, genuine good advice or warnings, just a quest direction for a village 20 Minutes away that somehow needs MY help specifically.

Talking to the toddlers gives a funny "Mama told me not to talk to strangers" dialogue, why does a 4-year old look like a 1-year old who just learned to walk...
Its a good medieval sim but building a house gave me RSI, so I gave up

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game suffers from multiplayer connection bugs, crashes, and server issues when trying to play co-op sessions.

citations.review_text: amazing. except the coop connection bugs
Great game, but the multiplayer is extremely buggy, constant lag and there is no way to fix it. I even tried to add it to bypass the firewall and such. Other than that, great game.

Enjoy the solo gameplay but cant recommend after spending almost 6 hours total over 3 days just trying to play co-op with my wife whom also enjoys the game.  Its hard to justify buying a game out of early access with bugs that have been known since 2024.  Unable to load character after spending 5 hours starting a village only for the character to be wiped from the face of the earth after going to bed irl and coming back the next day for the safe file to be fine but my character with everything on him gone like he had a heart attack overnight.  Multiple errors and crashes just trying to start the game for co-op just seems like a total mess.  Cant even request a refund now and just frustrating.

(Edit) Thank you for the quick responses,  it seems folks have had issues in the past but typically a result of conflicts with Steam ID.  Not an easy fix but simply starting from scratch fixed the issue.  From other issues this one seems less uncommon.  Recommend just based on the fact yall are there to assist and I appreciate that more then anything.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: As the world opens up, appreciation grows for the visuals and audio despite unguided openings and occasional multiplayer crashes.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features beautiful graphics, detailed environments, and a pleasant soundtrack.

citations.review_text: A great medival sim. Great graphics. Decent Mechanics. Would love if some trade realted upgrades are made in the future.
Absolutely amazing graphics, gameplay, and vibe. The soundtrack is beautiful and UI is easy to use.
super fun! very nice graphics, def peak

i love how medieval dynasty mixes town management with survival and also some drama! a lot of “kingdom management” games are top down, too confusing, or too in depth in the wrong places. this is so fun in every aspect! i love the scenery, super pretty! the ui isn’t confusing either, really easy to understand. there’s so much to do when you get bored of one task. i loveeee it!

I've been having a great time with Medieval Dynasty. The graphics look beautiful, and the game runs surprisingly well even on my gaming laptop with an RTX 3050 Ti (4 GB, 50W). It still looks great while maintaining smooth performance.

The atmosphere is one of the game's biggest strengths. The world feels alive thanks to random events, abandoned carts, bandit encounters, camps, and other small details that make exploration enjoyable.

Building your settlement is satisfying, and managing your village is fun without becoming overwhelming. Watching your little community grow over time is rewarding.

The hunting system deserves special praise. It's not just "shoot and collect." You need to stay hidden, think carefully about where you aim, and if you don't land a vital shot, you'll often have to track the animal by following its blood trail. Finally catching it feels genuinely rewarding.

The survival mechanics are also well balanced. Managing temperature, hunger, and thirst adds immersion without becoming frustrating or constantly getting in the way of gameplay.

Progression takes time, but it never feels like an exhausting grind. You always feel like you're making progress, which keeps the experience enjoyable.

The only thing I really miss is voice acting and a bit more life on the roads, such as traveling caravans or random NPCs passing by. That said, it's a small complaint because the world already feels alive thanks to all the random events.

Overall, if you enjoy medieval life sims, village building, survival, and exploration, I can definitely recommend Medieval Dynasty.
Fun game with an over the top (insanely over the top) skill tree you have to manage (and takes from game play), which is annoying. The rest of the game is amazing with great graphics.

Not bad I like the whole concept of poor to rich but dont get me wrong there is a lot of work that comes into building a civilization but Im loving every moment of it. The graphics are pretty good and I love the concept of relationships and building a dynasty to rule said civilization but I do wish there was more places to explore.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the early game as slow-paced and difficult, featuring tedious fetch quests and aggressive wildlife attacks right at the start.

citations.review_text: Terrible early game pacing and brain-dead mechanics. i thought it's some immersive medieval city builder, but the early game is an absolute joke. Instead of doing anything rewarding, you spend the first few hours marathon-running across the entire map for tedious fetch quests. To make it worse, the game throws hunting quests at you almost immediately without giving you the actual tools to complete them. It expects you to crouch around and somehow headshot a wild deer with a basic wooden spear. It makes no sense. Meanwhile, the aggressive wildlife behaves completely unrealistic, every single wolf and fox acts like it’s rabid and just blindly sprints to attack you on sight. The biggest red flag is that the developers literally put a built-in cheat engine right into the standard game settings. Having boxes for literal god mode, infinite stamina, and infinite health isn't a "feature", it’s a pathetic testimony that the developers know exactly how much their own awful combat and early game suck. Instead of fixing the tedious progression loops, they just gave the player the buttons to break the game. Honestly, I can’t even comment on whether the actual city-building or dynasty aspects of this game are fun or not. The game forces you to plow through so much mindless running and stupid, frustrating hunting quests right off the bat that I completely lost interest before my village could even get off the ground. Don't waste your time unless you enjoy glorified walking simulators with clunky arcade mechanics.

Medieval Dynasty... I can only describe this game in one phrase:

[b][i]I simply love it.[/i][/b]

One of the original games to popularize this style of "Dynasty" gameplay, Medieval Dynasty has inspired plenty of copy over the years. Judging by their reviews, though, it's safe to say that none of them have managed to beat the original. After 30 hours of playtime in just two weeks, I think I've spent enough time with it to leave a proper review.

[h2]The learning curve can be scary:[/h2]
I first discovered this game while it was still on Early Access on my Steam front page. I wasn't planning to buy it immediately because I wanted to see how it would develop first. So I added it to my wishlist and hoped it wouldn't become yet another abandoned survival game.

Looking at it now, I couldn't have been more wrong.

I first tried the game on the Xbox Game Pass but was met with disappointment when my hardware obviously couldn't handle it at the time. So, fair warning: you'll want a reasonably capable PC with decent hardware if you want to enjoy the game at its best.

When I finally bought it, I was immediately hooked.

It took quite a bit of a bit of a challenge on handling the learning curve considering how you're immediately plunged into the open world with no hand-holding at all. It's basically:

  [b] "Go out there and start grinding, you parentless peasant." [/b]

and I kid you not, it's one of the most intimidating feelings ever. But I took joy in that learning process, gave it my patience and time, without googling any tips like "How to build the Roman Empire in one day in Medieval Dynasty." It took me around 4.5 hours to really understand what I was doing, and as time went on I slowly felt the grind getting worse, but every restart taught me something new. What initially took me two hours eventually took only one, and by my third attempt I had learned from my mistakes enough to build a self-sufficient village that could run itself without constant babysitting.

[h2]…

I am very new to this type of genre, as I prefer to play more action-oriented games, with titles such as Warhammer, Total War, Gears of War, Resident Evil (ah, you name it) being played almost daily or whenever I have the time to play games.

But there's just something about this game that holds a very special place in my heart. It's probably the settings, ambience, music, and just the overall slow pacing that makes it so special (or perhaps, I'm just getting older).

Honestly, I thought the game was quite boring during the beginning phase, and I got lost since I had no idea on where to start. The game literally throws everything at you the moment you click on New Game, and I personally got lost having to deal with all the in-game mechanics and explanations, but after playing it slower and feeling the rhythm of it all, I actually LOVE this game.

Overall, Medieval Dynasty is a (VERY) nice change of pace from the usual games that I played, and I strongly recommend all of you to check it out. This is definitely a 10/10 for me.

claims.claim: Reviewers report experiencing random crashes during multiplayer sessions.

citations.review_text: Very nice experience, I never expected for a very slow game to get me so addicted to it. Occasional crashes when hosting multiplayer sessions but apart from that, 10/10 experience

So far this game has been great (about to start my 4th year in game), its a really good blend between a traditional city builder and a RPG game. So far I haven't played the campaign mode, just building my village in the Oxbow region, but even in the Oxbow region, you still have some quests to complete - all optional unless you want to unlock fast travel to your village. While most of the quests  in the Oxbow are simple, the dialog for the quests can be quite amusing.

Pros:

- Game seems to be generally bug free (for me, anyway). Had a couple game crashes, but its likely a system issue as I have that happen with other games too. 1 time the fertilizer I made disappeared, but other than that the only bug I encountered was my settlers kind of floating to their destination rather than walking.

- Managing settlers, buildings, and livestock is very straight forward. 

- Upgrading and/or moving building is easy

- Plenty of exterior aesthetics to make your village really look like a true medieval village

- Plenty of options to change the difficulty of the game, from the resources NPCs need to XP gains, enemy/animal damage and HP to whether or not you even need to eat/drink and more

- Being able to change how many days are in a season gives you plenty of time to do building and quests in between seasons; and after like 3 days you can just skip to the next season if you want.

Cons:

- The stats you can gain are somewhat limited. There's not much you can do to increase stats relating to combat, and all level caps are fairly limited as it is. Having stats for particular weapon types would be great, as would just having more levels to earn for the stats that are already in the game.

- By default the game limits the amount of buildings to 70. While this might seem reasonable, each orchard and field for crops counts as a building, if you don't start your settlement near larger areas of open land, you can easily reach that limit. The game does allow for yo…

claims.claim: Reviewers report that managing villagers and production limits involves a tedious, console-first interface that lacks copy settings options for buildings and requires tracking consumption across separate screens.

citations.review_text:
I want to like this game, i really do. Peaople in the review section will tell you all about adequate performance, decent visuals and all the good stuff. I'll tell you about the bad instead:

- The guy who designed villager designation system should be kept from influencing any player managed system ever freaking again. You split the "time" of your villagers between tasks, BUT you cant set the limit on how much they produce or how low they should go consuming something in the process. You may end up with a ton of goods you dont need
And to see how much you consume you have to move to a different screen, write down the number etc etc
The system is made worse by villagers skillupping and starting to produce more. And you have to constantly juggle values in a clearly console-first interface. People make excel spreadsheets to manage this mess! Its made even worse by women getting pregnant and leaving the worker pool for a few years and you replace her with someone else with a different skill level and here we go again...
The only system that works ok is farming. Coz it does not use the system above!
- You cant upgrade buildings to a higher tier and when you make new ones you have to set everything by hand again, coz you cant copy the settings...
- Building placement sometimes acts wonky
- When you dismount you end up looking away from your mount and not where you were looking before that. Sounds like a minor things, but annoying AF
- They highlight option you get cant be filtered, so if you decorate your village you will get HEAPS of text on screen
- No minimap, WHY?
- You cant place a table inside the house. Yeah...
- Some achievements dont trigger in coop (the one to spend the winter naked, for example). Some of them fail to register properly (like the one with stolen items counter) from time to time
- Some talents are what you can call "tax" talent. You have to pick em up or you will suffer. The one that calls your hourse, for example. The talents are, overall, unima…

130 hours later...

I bought this game thinking I'd be a rugged medieval hunter. Instead, I'm the HR department, city planner, carpenter, therapist, farmer, wildlife control officer, and the only person in the kingdom capable of cutting down a tree.

Every season starts the same:
"I'm just going to gather a little wood."

Three hours later I've accidentally built an entire industrial district, reorganized my villagers' jobs for the fifth time, and somehow still don't have enough sticks. The villagers are incredible. They'll happily produce 4,000 cabbages a year, but if you forget to assign someone to collect firewood, the whole town acts like winter was your personal decision.

Nothing humbles you quite like spending two in-game years building the perfect house, decorating it beautifully, then realizing you placed your whole home in the opposite direction of everyone else's. AND don't even get me started on carrying logs. One minute you're a respected village leader, the next you're waddling across the map at the speed of continental drift because you refused to make a second trip.

Bandits? Manageable.

Bears? Terrifying.

Trying to figure out why your blacksmith suddenly stopped making hammers? That's the real final boss.

This game somehow turned spreadsheets into entertainment. Every little improvement feels rewarding, and watching your tiny camp grow into a thriving medieval town is incredibly satisfying.

I came for survival.

I stayed because my flax production depends on me.

10/10. Now if you'll excuse me, my villagers are somehow out of buckets again.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game includes extensive customization settings that let players adjust difficulty, season lengths, and gameplay speeds to suit their preferences.

citations.review_text: I really love this game. It's simple with a mix of complexity. Medieval Dynasty knows the perfect blend of hard and easy, and that's just on the default world configs. I especially love how you can customize almost everything when making a new save AND even when in said world! This game is amazing for that, and also because of the general gameplay as well. 10/10, will recommend.

The game is great, it's easy to understand the mechanics, you can make it as easy or hard as you want with the game customization, you can go from hardcore survival mode to cosy chill game like that. You can also make seasons longer or shorter. 
If you like those medieval style city builder games and you wish you could be there in first person in that city you're building and craft and go on adventures... now you can
They also make tons of pop culture and gaming culture references with random NPC dialogs. 

An overall very joyful experience and I'll be playing again surely.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention encountering fatal errors and crashes that require a full reinstall to resolve.

citations.review_text:
Unexpectedly fun.  It's a slow burn (unless you ramp up the speed in the settings).  A lot more fun in Co-op.  I am currently playing the single player Valley map, and Oxbow with a friend.  Co-op feels like it has a lot more to offer in the long run.  We are really enjoying the game.  And nice to see a game released a few years ago, still has a roadmap for additional content.  

I have encountered fatal errors here and there, research recommends a full reinstall if the usual things don't fix it (eg GPU driver updates, verify files, etc.)  Seems to be Okay after a reinstall; not sure what triggers it as it happens with different activities in game.  Not too big of a deal, set autosave to 5 minutes, you don't lose any real progress.  You can also F5 to quicksave as well.  Doesn't happen enough to ragequit.

If you enjoy community building and games that have a pretty infinite end-game and enjoy a slow burn, this is probably for you.
Extremely unstable. Barely works. Constant crashes.
